sections.h2: When does the Alpena County recording desk take your deed?
sections.html:
The register works out of 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, and answers at 989-354-9547. According to the county office page, the counter is staffed Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Recording cutoffs come sooner than closing time. Electronic submissions count for the day only if they arrive by 3:30 p.m., and paper brought to the counter by 4:00 p.m. Later arrivals roll into the following business day's work, so a Friday 4:15 delivery waits until Monday.

The register insists on originals. After indexing, the paper goes back to whoever sent it, typically within a week of the recording date. Blank deed forms are not handed out at the desk, and staff will not coach you through filling one in; the page suggests an office supply store, a lawyer or a title company.

sections.h2: Which fees does Alpena County collect for recording and copies?
sections.html:
State law, MCL 600.2567, sets the schedule that most counties use: one flat charge per document, whatever its length. Only a charter county may adopt a different one by ordinance, so call the register to confirm the total before you mail a check.

  • $30 for each recorded paper, plus $3 for each additional instrument it assigns or discharges.
  • $1 a page for copies, $5 to certify.
  • 50 cents per year of grantor and grantee index searching, with a $5 floor.
  • A tax certification fee on certain deeds. Ask the Alpena County treasurer whether yours qualifies.

The office page links a fee sheet, recording requirements and e-recording instructions for anyone who wants the full detail.

sections.h2: What search and alert tools does the Alpena County register run?
sections.html:
Researchers can choose Laredo or Tapestry. Per the county, Tapestry fits someone who needs a copy or two, and Laredo suits title companies and frequent searchers.

Alpena County residents can also enroll in a free property fraud alert and a free notary fraud alert. Each one sends a call, text or email when a recorded document carries your name.

The same counter serves as a certified passport agent and takes passport photos, which is worth knowing if the line seems long.

sections.h2: What will state and county transfer tax cost on an Alpena County house?
sections.html:
Alpena County's median owner-occupied value is $153,900 for 2020 to 2024, per Census Bureau figures. That value fills 308 units of $500, and the seller owes $0.55 per unit to the county (MCL 207.504) and $3.75 per unit to the state (MCL 207.525).

Transfer tax on a $153,900 Alpena County sale (308 units of $500), worked from MCL 207.504 and 207.525
PartMathResult
County308 x $0.55$169.40
State308 x $3.75$1,155.00
Both308 x $4.30$1,324.40

The money goes to the Alpena County treasurer within 15 days of delivery. A sale that bundles in furniture or equipment is taxed on the real estate alone, provided the deed or an attached affidavit lists the two values apart.

sections.h2: Which distress and court transfers escape the Alpena County transfer tax?
sections.html:
Foreclosure outcomes, probate court actions and land contracts show up often in distressed sales, and MCL 207.526 addresses each.

  • Foreclosure, or a deed in lieu of foreclosure, on a mortgage. The lender's own later resale is taxed.
  • A transfer ordered by a court of record, unless the court sets a money price.
  • A land contract that leaves legal title with the seller until the price is fully paid.
  • A spouse-to-spouse conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties.

Paid in error? The Department of Treasury handles refund requests.

sections.h2: What details on a deed trip up an Alpena County recording?
sections.html:
The recording act, MCL 565.201, lists data a register looks for. Misses here cause most returns:

  • Signer names printed beneath each signature in black or dark blue ink, matching the notary acknowledgment.
  • The notary's printed name on the same page as the signature.
  • The buyer's address, and the drafter's name and business address.
  • Social Security numbers cut to their last four digits or less.
  • A written English translation attached to any foreign-language text.

A paper that meets the act cannot be rejected for its content.

sections.h2: How should you time a deed against the Alpena County cutoffs?
sections.html:
Start the e-record by early afternoon, because the 3:30 p.m. cutoff arrives half an hour before the counter's 4:00. Before signing, run through a short list:

  • The buyer's mailing address appears on the deed.
  • The notary's name is printed beside the signature.
  • The full sale value is stated, or a value affidavit is attached.
  • The original, not a copy, goes to the register.
  • Any tax certification step has been cleared with the county treasurer.

Miss the cutoff and your record date moves to the next business day.

sections.h2: What is Alpena County like for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
In the northeast of Michigan's Lower Peninsula, Alpena County fronts Lake Huron and Thunder Bay, and the Thunder Bay River drains most of its land. The legislature created it in 1840 as Anamickee County, renamed it in 1843, and organized it in 1857. The 45th parallel cuts across the county, and Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary lies offshore, with automated lighthouses on Middle Island and Thunder Bay Island.

Alpena is the only city and the seat of government. Hillman is a village shared with another county, and the rest of the settled places are Alpena Charter Township and Ossineke. U.S. 23 hugs the shoreline, M-32 ends in downtown Alpena, and M-65 offers a quicker way south.

Census Bureau estimates give 28,853 residents for mid-2025, a 0.2 percent slip from the 2020 base, with 27.9 percent aged 65 or more. About 80 percent of homes are owner occupied. Median household income is $53,950, the mean commute is 17.5 minutes, and median gross rent is $673. In 2023 the county counted 822 employer establishments and 10,141 jobs, and its 2022 retail sales reached about $616 million.

Assessments are a local matter, so a seller with a parcel question should call the city or township assessor, not the register.

sections.h2: How have Alpena County's population and housing changed over time?
sections.html:
The head count peaked at 32,315 in 1980, fell to 30,605 in 1990, and stood at 29,598 in 2010 and 28,907 in 2020.

The 2020 to 2024 Census data counts 13,019 households with 2.17 people each and 15,768 housing units as of 2025. Owners with a mortgage carry median monthly costs of $1,096, and owners without one pay $455. Poverty affects 16.7 percent of residents, and 18.3 percent of adults 25 or older hold a bachelor's degree.

The land itself is part of the story. Glaciers left a Grayling outwash plain of sandy ridges, jack pine barrens and hardwood forest, and large inland lakes such as Long Lake and Grand Lake sit north of the city along U.S. 23.

faqs.q: When does the Alpena County Register of Deeds stop accepting recordings?
faqs.a: Paper and walk-in filings stop at 4:00 p.m., and e-recordings at 3:30 p.m. Anything later is handled the next business day.

faqs.q: How do I phone the Alpena County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call 989-354-9547, or fax 989-354-9646. The office sits at 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, in Alpena.

faqs.q: Does the Alpena County register hand back my original deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the paper is indexed, the office returns it, usually inside a week of recording.

faqs.q: What is the total transfer tax on a $153,900 Alpena County sale?
faqs.a: It is $1,324.40, made up of $1,155.00 for the state and $169.40 for the county. Each is charged per $500 or fraction of $500.

faqs.q: Will Alpena County staff draft my deed or advise on it?
faqs.a: No. Staff do not complete documents, give legal advice or supply blank deeds. Go to a title company, an attorney or an office supply store.
